content.title: How to watch the Detroit Tigers vs San Diego Padres on new network Detroit SportsNet
content.text: LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — The Detroit Tigers’ season begins on Thursday with a road series against the San Diego Padres. Detroit’s ace Tarik Skubal will face San Diego’s Nick Pivetta. Thursday’s game will start at 4:10 p.m. ET, while Friday’s game is at 9:40 p.m. and Saturday’s is at 8:40 p.m. All three games will air on Detroit SportsNet, a new channel that replaces Main Street Sports Group’s FanDuel Sports Network Detroit. Tigers announcer Jason Benetti will continue to call games for the team, though Benetti will miss Thursday’s game to call a game between the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers and the Arizona Diamondbacks. Tigers radio announcer Dan Dickerson will call the Tigers’ first game of the season. Detroit SportsNet will be available via pay-TV packages, including Xfinity and Spectrum, and via a streaming app. The full list of networks published on Thursday included digital streaming pay-TV provider FuboTV, but did not include YouTube TV, Hulu Live TV, or Dish Network. It’s unclear if pay-TV subscribers would be charged a “regional sports fee,” which cable providers added to customers’ bills to offset the high carriage fees charged by regional sports networks, including FanDuel Sports Network and NBC Sports Network’s regional networks in cities like Chicago and Philadelphia. The high costs of RSNs led Dish Network and YouTube TV to avoid paying for these networks altogether, and often meant that RSNs would be unavailable for short periods on some pay-TV providers because contracts would lapse during negotiations. The Detroit SportsNet streaming app uses MLB TV’s streaming infrastructure to broadcast Detroit Tigers games, with Red Wings coming at the start of next season. Fans can purchase a subscription for $19.99 per month or $189.99 per year. Out-of-market Tigers fans can still watch games with a standard MLB TV subscription for $29.99 per month, while out-of-market Red Wings fans can watch games with an ESPN+ subscription.
